It happens once a year, is known well in advance, and work takes place between the police, loyal orders and others to ensure it is safe and respectful. Kimmins language is in stark contrast to the mutual respect shown during the Fleadh, despite a week of traffic disruption and local traders losing business to pop up stalls.  Unionists, including me, attended events, bands participated enthusiastically and different traditions celebrated together. The Belfast Bands Forum participated in the Fleadg - holding one of the best events of the week at Titanic Slipways.  We should always minimise disruption and maximise opportunities for local traders during major events. I know the loyal orders share that ambition, and I have engaged with them in Londonderry to support local businesses during the Apprentice Boys parade when I was policing there.  In a democracy, different communities celebrate their culture in different ways. This intervention sounds like a reaction to the Parades Commission being exposed as incompetent. We need to address that and not flex to parading tensions.  Mutual respect must work both ways and Liz Kimmons should be focused on sorting the potholes that disrupt us all every day of the week.

caption: Great speech from Andy Burnham on Monday. But how could maximum devolution work in practice? Last year I asked Andy Burnham to spell it out in Parliament - where he trailed the idea of local control of labour market policy for the under-25s.  That became part of a series of recommendations we made. The theory is simple. The UK is running an output gap - but that varies regionally. So, we need far more devolution of labour market policy and investment to help ensure very part of Britain is firing on all cylinders. Combine that with a ‘total place’ approach to pooled regional budgets to help transform the local state.  Our key advice:  1.Skills as the proving ground. Post-16 technical education should be devolved to leaders who can commission it against the real strengths of their economy. Andy Burnham has made this case for years. The evidence backs him. 2.Devolved growth needs devolved capital. We called for British Business Bank branches in every mayoral region and a real pipeline of investable propositions. A region with its own growth plan needs a visible route to the money that funds it. 3. That should be part of a rebuild of regional banking. Bring together British Business Bank and Post Office banking hubs to put small business banking on the high street. Radically expand state-backed lending guarantees. Back it up with Community Reinvestment Act to get major banks to lean in.  4.A place-based delivery spine. Mayors should sit inside the national strategy machinery, not next to it. One table, one set of numbers, national and regional leadership together. 5. Shift the capability. Mayors told us their single biggest constraint is in-house capacity. We recommended a secondment pool from the Treasury, the Department for Business and Trade and the British Business Bank, placed directly into mayoral authorities. The argument for devolution has been won. The work now is to make it deliver.
videoSummary: Liam Byrne MP explains his proposals for implementing maximum devolution across the UK to address regional economic gaps. He advocates for local control of labour market policies, skills training, and regional banking to empower mayors and stimulate growth.

caption: Ambition - not amnesia - is what Britain needed yesterday. And that’s exactly what the Chancellor delivered in this Budget. In Parliament yesterday, I set out why this Budget gets the big calls right. Despite a difficult inheritance, it charts a path for rising growth this year, rising business investment, falling inflation, falling interest rates, falling energy bills - and a collapse in child poverty. In my own constituency alone, 8,900 kids will be better off because of this Labour Budget. But the deeper point is this: after travelling the country with the Business & Trade Committee, the message from firms has been overwhelming. Britain is an inventive nation standing at the threshold of a new era of innovation - but to win the race for the 21st century we must: • Deliver certainty for business - ending the biannual fiscal circus. • Mobilise capital at scale: a revolution in ‘UKDI’ - from EMI company eligibility and VCT expansion to new UK listing relief. • Improve the return on investment - from internationally competitive energy costs to lower business rates and better, more coordinated regulation. For too long, Britain suffered from a trillion pounds of wasted debt, a collapse in productivity growth, and rising inequality.  Today’s Budget begins the long work of putting that right - and unlocking our potential as one of the best places in the world to invent, start, and scale a business. Our Committee will scrutinise every detail in the weeks ahead. But the signal today was clear: Britain can win this century - if we back our ingenuity with real investment and real ambition.

caption: Net Zero is not solving climate change - it is transferring emissions from Britain to elsewhere. Shutting down our refineries gets us closer to Net Zero. But then we import more diesel from India, with twice the emissions. Shutting down our oil and gas production in the North Sea get us closer to Net Zero. But then we import more gas from the other side of the world, with four times the emissions. Shutting down our factories gets us closer to Net Zero. But then we import the same goods back from China, where they’ve been made with coal. Each one increases GLOBAL emissions, but is counted as a success for our Net Zero targets. I would remind those criticising us on climate that we are the only party with a policy to measure the offshoring of emissions. We need to make electricity cheap, protect British industry, and focus on innovating the clean tech that will actually cut emissions around the world.

caption: I’m speaking to people who want more than the same old politics. They want new leadership and real change. Yesterday, I spoke to a hardworking woman who works six days a week, pays her taxes and plays by the rules -  yet she feels the system is working against her. Her ex-husband avoids paying child maintenance by working cash in hand, leaving no proper record of his earnings. She reports it to Benefit Fraud and the Child Maintenance Service, but nothing seems to happen. I hear stories like this far too often. Those who work hard, pay their taxes and do the right thing should not be ignored while others exploit the system or avoid their responsibilities. Of course, we must always support those who genuinely cannot work because of illness, disability or vulnerability. I volunteered for a foodbank myself and I’m passionate about supporting people.  That is what a compassionate society does. But compassion must go hand in hand with fairness, responsibility and firm action against fraud.  Working people deserve a government that is on their side - one that listens, acts and delivers. 🔵 A FAIR DEAL FOR WORKING PEOPLE. 🔵 NEW LEADERSHIP. REAL CHANGE.

caption: Northern Ireland has a world-class workforce and world-class businesses and I am determined to celebrate, promote and support them. On Friday, I had the privilege of visiting Encirc, the glassDiana Armstrong MLAt in Fermanagh, alongside Diana Armstrong MLA, Deputy Leader of the Ulster Unionist Party. Diana is our economy spokesperson and herself a entrepreneur.  Encirc is a truly global success story. The company produces billions of bottles every year and is leading the way in environmentally responsible glass manufacturing. Their innovation and commitment to sustainability place them at the cutting edge of the industry. Here’s something many people don’t realise - every single bottle of Baileys sold anywhere in the world is made right here in Fermanagh at Encirc. No matter where you see it, in an airport, supermarket or bar across the globe it started in Northern Ireland. That’s something we can all be proud of. Diana and I listened carefully to the management team and discussed forthcoming legislation, including the proposed Good Jobs Bill. It is our job to ensure our Executivecreates the right conditions for businesses and workers to flourish. Too often, Stormont has done the opposite. We must do better. Recently, I also visited the Old Bushmills Distillery, another world-class company with deep roots in our history and a global reputation for excellence. It was fitting to visit a business producing many of the bottles for their renowned whiskey soon after.  Northern Ireland has the talent, the ambition and the natural strengths to succeed. I am proud of our businesses, proud of our workforce, and proud of our people. The Ulster Unionist Party will continue to champion Northern Ireland - supporting enterprise, backing workers, and ensuring we create the conditions for everyone to flourish.

caption: Banking hubs are a vital lifeline for our communities. They offer far more than just cash access or standard Post Office services – providing essential face-to-face financial advice, support with fraud and scams, and assistance with complex issues like power of attorney.  Yet, with over 200 bank branches set to close across the country this year, we are starting to see banking deserts becoming more common across the country.  In Mid Derbyshire, the last bank closed in Allestree Park Farm in 2018, and in Spondon it has been without a bank for around a decade. This is despite having thriving highstreets that would greatly benefit from the additional footfall banks provide.  We have also seen the tremendous impact a banking hub can have in Mid Derbyshire. The Belper Banking Hub is extraordinarily popular, as the hub supports between 1,450 and 1,650 customer interactions each week.  I believe both Allestree and Spondon deserve access to these essential financial services. It would help boost their local highstreets, increasing footfall and supporting local businesses. As post offices already operate from these communities, a Banking Hub would work in partnership with them and upgrade the services they already provide.  Residents have spoken to me about their interest in this. I have written to the Head of Financial Inclusion at LINK to make the case for banking hubs in both communities. If you have a view on a banking hub in Allestree or Spondon, please let me know your thoughts on this as it will help me make the case to LINK about improving banking services in your local area.  #highstreet #community #banking #bankinghub

caption: 🏊‍♂️ Boston Spa dives into my 𝗔𝘂𝗴𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘃𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗵𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 of Wetherby & Easingwold... The village of Boston Spa began as a #spa resort linked to Thorp Arch, before the one-time retreat outgrew its neighbour and was given its modern name in 1850. Boston’s story began in 1744 with John Shires’ discovery of sulphur springs in the magnesian limestone bank of the River Wharfe. Shires would open the mineral pools of “Thorp Spaw” to capture the growing spa craze of the Georgian and later Victorian period. In 1753, Joseph Taite built the first hotel, The Farrier’s Hotel (later The Royal, now Costcutter) on the main highway that would become known as “Bostongate” (now High Street) by 1799. With more than 600 residents, the emerging village was called “Boston” in 1822. The name is believed to originate from local landowners with a Lincolnshire connection. By 1834, dedicated spa buildings were built on the riverside, complete with hot and cold baths, a pump room and a tearoom for refreshments. At its peak in the mid-1800s, there were more than 50 visitors to the spa every day. The spa would eventually close in the late 1960s following spa tourism’s decline. caption: 🌟 Redditch: £20 Million Investment to Transform Greenlands and Woodrow! 🌟 For too long, communities like Greenlands and Woodrow have been left behind and forgotten. That’s finally changing. caption: 🧑‍🌾🐖 ONE DAY TO GO – DRIFFIELD SHOW 150!  As we look forward to tomorrow’s agriculture show, did you know that 40% of all English pigs are raised on farms here in East Yorkshire and the Humber – bringing in £499 million in an industry ultimately worth £7 billion in retail sales to the UK economy?  Unfortunately, an oversupply of as many as 100,000 pigs relative to demand, rising costs from the conflict in the Middle East, and falling EU prices leading to a 15% drop in prices, has meant that some farmers are recently losing as much as £50 per pig.  Many supermarkets and processors have therefore been giving notice on their contracts with farms – including with farmers right here in East Yorkshire who have been in touch with me – putting jobs and livelihoods at serious risk.  So, having already written to the previous Secretary of State for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs on this, I also raised it with her directly when she appeared before the EFRA Select Committee. We will always be a kind and compassionate country, but we do need to be one that isn’t taken advantage of because twinned with a cost of living crisis it has led to some real divisions in our society and stoked a kind of racism that I hoped was kicked to the kerb in the 80s. Julie highlighted how pupils from Cauldwell School, Grange Academy School, King’s Oak Primary School, Priory Primary School, Queen’s Park Academy, and The PLACE Programme will come together on Wednesday 1 July 2026 (12–2pm) at Bedford Market for a special Young Marketeers celebration, selling the produce they’ve grown over the past six months. It was brilliant to hear how the programme is supporting children to develop practical life skills, confidence around food, and a better understanding of healthy eating with clear evidence showing the long-term benefits of strong food education. caption: This is the wrong tax at the wrong time and yet another attack by Labour on Britain’s tourism and hospitality industry. Tourism is a British success story. It generates more than £147 billion in economic activity, supports millions of jobs and brings more than £30 billion a year into Britain from overseas visitors. Yet since Labour’s first Budget, more than 100,000 jobs have already been lost across tourism and hospitality. Instead of asking how they can help this vital sector grow, Labour’s answer is yet another tax. I warned Ministers in Parliament that even a £2 per person per night charge would add £56 to the cost of a week-long holiday for a family of four. For many families that is significant, particularly for lower-cost breaks and caravan holidays where it could represent a substantial increase in the overall price. Now we discover that Labour has not even put a cap on the tax. We all know what happens with taxes like this: they start at one level and then go up and up. Businesses and holidaymakers are being handed a blank cheque with no certainty about how high the charge could eventually become. This comes on top of higher National Insurance costs, business rates pressures, rising employment costs and all the other burdens Labour has already imposed on businesses. What does this Labour Government have against tourism? We should be encouraging families to holiday in Britain, attracting more international visitors and helping our hotels, B&Bs, caravan parks and visitor attractions to grow and create jobs. Instead, Labour is making holidays more expensive and Britain less competitive. And there is still a fundamental question about where this money will actually go. If people are being charged a tourism tax, there must at the very least be an absolute guarantee that every penny raised is spent supporting tourism, rather than disappearing into wider council budgets. The Conservatives would take the opposite approach. We would back hospitality, tourism and leisure businesses with 100% business rates relief and help them invest, employ people and grow. You cannot tax your way to growth, and Labour cannot keep hammering one of Britain’s most important industries and expect it to thrive. #ukpolitics #tourismtax @Conservatives @UKHospitality

caption: 🚨Labour and Lib Dem MPs just voted to INCREASE the cost of energy, food, shipping, housing, heating and holidays by voting for Ed Miliband’s new Net Zero target. One of the reasons I asked to stay in this brief was my time in the Department and seeing how badly we were making decisions about climate and energy. There’s simply no scrutiny or proper analysis of what these targets are doing to jobs, the cost of living or to the competitiveness of our industry. The Minister bringing it forward refused to take a single intervention. She did not answer a single question. I’m sorry, but that is simply not good enough. MP after MP cited bogus figures or praised the Climate Change Committee’s analysis without being even slightly troubled that their cost of offshore wind was wrong by a factor of three. Get the cost of energy wrong and all your other assumptions about the cost of living and the economy will be wrong too. I am proud Kemi Badenoch and I have changed our party’s position. We are the only party who have said we should measure the offshoring of emissions. We are the only party who have a plan to make electricity cheaper without costing the taxpayer a penny. We are the only party with a fully costed plan to axe the Carbon Tax which is replacing clean British industry with dirtier foreign imports. This debate shows why Parliament is not working. Poor analysis let off the hook by poor scrutiny. So-called impact assessments which are written to be as impenetrable as possible, and which MPs show no interest in reading or questioning. We need fewer virtue signalling MPs and many more who can read modelling assumptions. #fyp #ukpolitics
videoSummary: Claire Coutinho delivers a direct critique of the government’s recent Net Zero policy, arguing that it lacks sufficient scrutiny and will negatively impact the economy and cost of living. She contrasts these decisions with the Conservative party's current policy approach, highlighting their plans for energy costs and the offshoring of emissions.

A vast royal hunting ground for boar and deer, the forest stretched northward from the ancient city walls of #York , taking in Easingwold and Sheriff Hutton. Tollerton was one of the entrances to the forest. Travellers could pay for an armed guide to protect them from outlaws and thieves as they passed through. In 1629, the royal Forest of Galtres began to be disafforested to raise urgent funds for King Charles I. The only confrontation in #Shakespeare 's Henry IV, Part II was in "Gaultree Forest". Describing the 1405 Northern Rising, the short-lived rebel force of 8,000 men mustered on Shipton Moor near Tollerton. Like Tollerton itself, the forest's name survives today with the Easingwold Galtres Centre and Forest of Galtres Golf Club too. 𝘞𝘩𝘪𝘤𝘩 𝘷𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘐 𝘩𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘭𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘯𝘦𝘹𝘵? caption: ⛪ Roecliffe vaults into my 𝗔𝘂𝗴𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘃𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗵𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 of Wetherby & Easingwold... Meaning "red bank or cliff" in Old Norse, the village of Roecliffe's clay pits supplied the village's brick and tile production works until the Sixties. Built of local limestone and roof tiles, St Mary's Church, Roecliffe opened in 1844. The neo-Norman #church is believed to be the only one in England with an entirely vaulted roof. St Mary's roof shape is known as a barrel, wagon or wagon-head design. The church's vestry door, marble flooring and chancel steps from the high altar pavement all came from York Minster as the cathedral was renovated following a fire in 1859. It is maintained by The Churches Conservation Trust and Boroughbridge Churches hold fortnightly services in the church. 𝘞𝘩𝘪𝘤𝘩 𝘷𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘴𝘩𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘐 𝘩𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘭𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘯𝘦𝘹𝘵? caption: At our fourth stop on the BTC road trip, and the conversations at The University of Sheffield AMRC highlight a common theme we’ve seen on the road so far: certainty and stability aren’t just nice to have - they’re a competitive advantage for the UK if we get them right. Businesses are clear that infrastructure matters, but it’s not just about the big headline projects. Getting the smaller, everyday pieces right, and building energy infrastructure to bring costs down, makes a real difference. People remain at the heart of the discussion - getting the right talent, building effective apprenticeship pipelines, and managing the impact of labour costs and national insurance contributions. Investment is moving in the right direction, but questions remain about how R&D tax credits can best incentivise the uptake of new technologies, particularly AI. Scale-up finance is still a bottleneck, operating costs remain high, and red tape continues to slow progress. Businesses want more red carpet, less red tape. Public procurement, export finance, and navigating the platform economy all came up as levers to drive growth, but SMEs are worried about some platforms making the landscape uncompetitive. Regional governance matters too: devolution of economic power and a clear regional mission will help ensure investment is strategic, targeted, and effective. Thanks to those who attended the Sheffield roundtable, I’m now calling on business leaders to fill in our questionnaire in my bio. Your insight will feed into our priorities report for the BTC 2026 work-plan, helping shape policies that support growing businesses, regional economies, and the wider UK economy. #IndustrialPolicy #BusinessGrowth #RegionalInvestment #TalentDevelopment #apprenticeships

caption: I asked the government this week about what plans they have to look at extending support for low-income households on heating oil. I welcomed the £53 million package which was announced to offer immediate help to these households, but should high prices continue throughout the year, which looks very probable, the government will likely need to do more. Minister for Energy Consumers Martin McCluskey responded, noting that the decision was taken to prioritise speed of delivery over a more extensive scheme. It took the government two and a half weeks to deliver this support, which he compared to the 200 days that the Tories took to provide support from the energy shock following the invasion of Ukraine. caption: Today in Parliament I raised the case of NDT Equipment Ltd, a small business in our constituency, over upcoming changes to steel tariffs. I visited the company, where the director Dan Lenton showed me the ultrasonic test calibration blocks and reference pieces they make and supply to manufacturers across a wide range of sectors, in the UK and abroad. Their precision measuring devices help ensure the safety of submarines, support the construction of nuclear power stations, and aid the development of high-end alloy production. This is serious, safety-critical work. The difficulty is the grade of steel they rely on, which is EN3B. There is no other manufacturer of this material at the quality required in the UK. This grade of steel the company uses should be exempt from the tariffs. I appreciate that the tariffs are needed to maintain British production of steel, but the needs of small and growing companies like this must also be taken into account. I’m meeting the Minister soon to discuss this further.

caption: GSK has today announced its intention to close its Stevenage site by 2029 and move operations to its Cambridge and Ware sites. Although GSK has stated jobs are being transferred rather than cut, and they are making further investment in our region, this is still disappointing news for Stevenage. I am also deeply frustrated by the lack of meaningful engagement from GSK before these plans were announced, which has caused unnecessary uncertainty for employees and the wider community. My first concern is with all GSK staff and families affected in Stevenage. While roles are set to move to sites that are commutable from Stevenage, this will still mean disruption for a significant number of people. They must be properly supported throughout this process, and I will be speaking with GSK staff and their representatives to ensure their interests come first. My other concern is for the research and business communities that might be affected by GSK’s move. We need to ensure that our wider research and tech industries are fully supported following GSK's move. I will use my role as our MP to bring them together and get the reassurances they need. Finally we need to make the best possible use of the GSK site after 2029. The generations of expertise in our town mean this site will be a great opportunity for those who can see its huge potential. So I will join the council and other Stevenage partners in banging the drum for major new investment there. What happens next is for us to decide, together. I know we will rise to this challenge.

caption: Redditch United FC has proudly announced that it is now officially carbon neutral, becoming what is believed to be only the second football club in the world to reach this major environmental milestone. Working with Neutral Carbon Zone, the club completed a full assessment of all its activities during the 2023–24 season, from energy use and travel to supply chains and day-to-day operations. caption: Last week I spoke in a debate on the importance of early diagnosis for women suffering with endometriosis and adenomyosis.  Endometriosis is a condition where endometrial tissue, similar to the lining of the uterus, grows in other places such as the ovaries and fallopian tubes. One in 10 women of reproductive age suffer with it, making it the second most common gynaecological condition in the UK. It shockingly takes on average 9 years for a diagnosis.  Adenomyosis, an often overlooked condition, has similar symptoms, but is where the lining of the womb starts growing into the muscle in the wall of the womb.  Again diagnosis often takes many years.  Endometriosis and adenomyosis can be dehabilitating conditions causing chronic pain and regular absence from school and work. They impact every aspect of a woman’s life.  Community diagnostic centres play an important role in providing much needed diagnostic scans for early diagnosis. I am delighted that we now have one in The Belfry in Redhill town centre, which will help diagnose conditions like these as well as many others. #endometriosis #adenomyosis #cdc #politics #conservatives
videoSummary: Rebecca Paul discusses her recent parliamentary contributions regarding the necessity of early diagnosis for endometriosis and adenomyosis. caption: 🏰 Crayke is my next 𝗔𝘂𝗴𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝘃𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗵𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 of Wetherby & Easingwold... Deriving its name from the Brittonic for "prominent crag", the Northumbrians granted Crayke to the growing #Christian #church in 685 and St Cuthbert subsequently built a monastery here. The Bishops of Durham would later build the first Crayke #Castle on top of the monastery in Norman times. The present fortified tower house was built in ~1450, having the neighbouring St Cuthbert's Church been dedicated to him in 1436. Crayke Castle was sold off by the Bishopric in 1827, but the parish fiercely defended remaining a detached part of County Durham. However, the parishioners' claim – and an exemption from North Riding taxes – was defeated in court in 1844. The Durham Ox, Crayke has stood at the foot of Church Hill for ~300 years The pub name is likely inspired by the founding legend of the City of Durham involving milkmaids guiding Cuthbert's followers and the famous 1.75-tonne Shorthorn cow that lived between 1796 and 1807. caption: The political and media noise in Northern Ireland has been getting worse in recent weeks, not better. Meanwhile, the issues that will actually determine our future rarely receive the passionate attention they deserve. The cost-of-living pressures and lack of affordable childcare that leave working families wondering whether their effort is genuinely rewarded. The prospect of a falling and ageing population, and what that means for our economy, public services and future. A failing wastewater system that prevents homes being built in more than 100 places, forcing people away from their families and driving up house prices and rents. The same infrastructure crisis is stopping businesses from expanding and creating jobs. A painfully slow planning system that frustrates investment and prevents businesses and farmers from growing. A brain drain caused by the lack of a proper skills pipeline and enough university places for our own young people. Leaving Northern Ireland should be a choice, not a necessity - and those who leave should have opportunities worth returning for. How we harness artificial intelligence, with the right ethical guardrails, to create wealth, improve productivity and secure good jobs. A justice system so slow that it lets down those who need it most, with victims losing hope and dropping out. An economic inactivity rate of around 26%, the highest in the United Kingdom and entirely unsustainable. It also means limited support is stretched more thinly, making it harder to help those who genuinely cannot work. A properly connected transport system - and the basic assurance that, if you choose the train, there will actually be somewhere to park. I could go on. Northern Ireland has achieved a great deal. We have world-class businesses, outstanding workers, thriving industries and enormous potential. But too much of that progress has happened in spite of our politics over the past 20 years, not because of it.
videoSummary: This carousel presents a detailed critique of the political and media noise surrounding Northern Ireland, shifting focus toward core systemic issues like cost-of-living pressures, infrastructure failures, and economic inactivity. Using structured text graphics and bold headings, the layout outlines specific socioeconomic challenges while highlighting the region's untapped potential and the need for future-focused solutions. The overall design combines professional editorial typography with symbolic imagery to advocate for substantive policy attention over political distraction.

caption: This week is Parliament Week, and I've been answering questions from students across Rugby about how politics actually works. Jacob from Rugby Free Secondary School asked me a direct question: why aren't we taxing the rich? The answer is straightforward. We are. The UK operates a progressive tax system. This means we don't apply the same tax rate to everyone regardless of income. That might sound fair on the surface, but it's not. A flat rate or poll tax approach hits people on lower incomes far harder. They end up paying a much larger proportion of what they earn compared to those who are better off. Our progressive system ensures that people with broader shoulders contribute more. Those earning higher incomes pay substantially more in tax. That's not just policy. It's fairness in action. You can read the full article and watch the complete conversation on Substack: https://substack.com/home/post/p-179555648

caption: New Bilton residents know the impact of HMO over-concentration. I've heard your concerns about litter, parking, antisocial behaviour and the fundamental change to our community. When I served as a councillor in New Bilton Ward, I campaigned on this issue and called for an Article 4 direction. Residents told me how family homes were being transformed into properties housing 4, 5, 6 or more residents. This often means that there are more cars needing parking space. They came before the planning committee to express these concerns, but they didn't count as material planning considerations. People feel powerless as their community is transformed. The previous Conservative administration failed to address HMOs in Rugby's local plan. Everything defaulted to national policy. The current Labour-led council has introduced an Article 4 direction and a radius-based approach in the draft plan, which should help. I spoke in Parliament this week to highlight these issues and asked ministers to look at new powers through the Planning and Infrastructure Bill. This is about empowering local communities and enabling them to have pride in their place. Please don't hesitate to get in touch if you have concerns about HMOs in your area.

caption: Why as Industry Minister am I pushing through the steel nationalisation bill? Because steel is not just another industry. It is one of the industries on which the whole country depends. That was true in 1948. It was true in 1966. And it is true now. I’ve spent my life in steel and industry, so I know this clearly: when productivity falls, when investment dries up and when government looks the other way, communities pay the price. That is exactly what happened under the previous Government. So we are acting:  - Backing a new Steel Strategy with up to £2.5 billion of financing this Parliament aiming to increase the share of UK steel demand met by UK producers to up to 50%, up from around 30%  - Tightening trade protections from 1 July 2026, cutting tariff-free import quotas by 60% and applying 50% tariffs above those levels on products that can be made here  - Strengthening procurement rules so government buyers must consult the UK Steel Digital Catalogue and consider national security when buying steel for public contracts This Bill is part of that bigger change. Laying the groundwork to boost productivity, bring in investment and regrow the steel industry. Steel built Britain. Now Britain needs to back steel again. #stocktonontees #Teesside #Steel #BritishIndustry #LabourDelivery

caption: Royal Mail Failures Over the past few years, postal services out of the Ashington sorting office have deteriorated significantly and have now reached the point of absurdity. Responsibility for this situation lies squarely with those running Royal Mail. It has been apparent for some time that, despite repeated assurances to the contrary, sorting offices across the country are operating well below minimum staffing levels. Hardworking postal workers are routinely instructed to prioritise parcels over letters and are effectively being sent out to fail in their duties. It is my firm belief that this is part of a deliberate strategy by Royal Mail to pressure the Government into weakening or scrapping the Universal Service Obligation. In the last week alone, I have received reports of birthday cards arriving weeks late, urgent changes to hospital appointments being missed, dozens of items of mail being delivered together after weeks of receiving nothing, a Christmas present finally turning up months after it was sent, and letters from the beginning of 2025 only now reaching their destination. This is completely unacceptable. Nor is it a new problem. These failures have been occurring for a considerable period of time. Earlier this year, I secured an Urgent Question in the House of Commons on Royal Mail's performance and was struck by the number of colleagues from across the country who reported experiencing exactly the same issues in their own constituencies. The Business and Trade Committee has worked diligently to hold Royal Mail to account and expose these failures, yet the situation continues to worsen. Staff in sorting offices such as Ashington are at breaking point. They need immediate support to tackle the backlog of mail and long-term investment to ensure these failures do not continue. Royal Mail should never have been allowed to pass into private ownership, where the pursuit of profit from parcel deliveries can take precedence over an essential public service. Hundreds of people are now being let down every week by a postal system they rely upon. It is time for the Government to step in, bring this critical service back into public ownership, and remove those profiteers who continue to ignore legitimate public concerns while standards continue to decline. #royalmail  #publicownership #post

It's decency and renewal with Labour or division and decline with our opponents.  This is a significant moment, akin to the rebuilding of our great country after the Second World War. It took hard work, sacrifice and grit then, and it will require the same now. The decisions ahead won't be easy, and there will be difficult moments. At the conference, there was a huge amount of optimism and confidence. The best days remain ahead of us. Together we can build a fairer and more prosperous economy, society and country for everybody. caption: This evening, we had a statement on the job losses at Exxon Mobil part of #Mossmorran. The key points are below and the statement (and questions) can be viewed here: https://youtu.be/qcfum6Q12og 1. Closure Announcement & Impact Exxon Mobil will close its Fife Ethylene Plant (#FEP) at Mossmorran, affecting 179 employees, 250 contractors, and the wider supply chain. Shell’s adjacent plant will not be impacted. 2. Reasons for Closure The plant is 40 years old, inefficient, and would require nearly $1 billion in investment to modernize. Combined with declining ethane supply and a challenging petrochemicals market, the site has been loss-making for five years, making continued operation commercially unviable. 3. Government’s Role & Limitations The UK Government engaged extensively with #ExxonMobil to explore options but concluded that the level of support required was beyond acceptable limits. Unlike other interventions (steel, shipbuilding), this case lacked a sound business proposition. 4. Support for Workers & Community The Government will provide assistance through the Department for Work and Pensions and PACE, and is engaging with unions (#Unite, #GMB). ExxonMobil has committed to supporting staff, including relocation opportunities to its Fawley site. 5. Future Industrial Strategy & Local Commitment The closure does not reflect UK industry’s overall health. The Government remains committed to industrial growth, citing £250 billion in investment and 45,000 jobs supported since July. Plans include promoting the Mossmorran site for future industrial investment and ensuring proper decommissioning. #EdinburghSouthWest
videoSummary: Dr Scott Arthur delivers a formal address regarding the closure of the Exxon Mobil plant at Mossmorran, detailing the impact on staff and the reasons behind the decision. The video outlines government support for the affected workers while clarifying why intervention was not feasible in this specific commercial case.
name: Scott Arthur

Labour MPs voting to block drilling of North Sea oil and gas, then weakening sanctions on Putin’s Russian oil, shows many Labour MPs just don’t get it. So I’ll continue to build on today’s productive meeting, to make sure Labour Ministers understand the importance of Atwick and Aldborough for Britain’s energy security and independence.

caption: 🚨 WE’RE BUILDING A MOVEMENT TO SCRAP COUNCIL TAX 🚨 Council Tax is one of the most unfair taxes in Britain. It’s based on property values from 1991. Yes, 1991. That’s why a Band D home in Wandsworth pays around £1,020 a year, while a Band D home in Hartlepool pays £2,556. Hard-working people in northern towns are paying more, while wealthier areas often pay less. It’s upside down, and it’s got to change. That’s why one of the very first things I did after arriving in Parliament was establish the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Council Tax Reform. Since then, we’ve been building a serious cross-party movement to replace this broken system with a fair proportional property tax. For Hartlepool, the difference would be transformational. ✅ Every household would pay less. ✅ The average family would save around £950 a year. ✅ Wealth would be redistributed so Councils would finally get the funding they need without forcing local people to shoulder an unfair burden. This isn’t about left or right. It’s about right and wrong. People in Hartlepool shouldn’t be punished simply because of where they live. The campaign is growing. MPs from across the country are joining the fight. Now let’s finish the job and scrap Council Tax once and for all.
videoSummary: Jonathan Brash MP explains his campaign to scrap Council Tax, arguing the current system is outdated and unfairly disadvantages residents in northern towns. caption: Today's announcement that Government will work towards public acquisition of Speciality Steel UK is a landmark moment for Stocksbridge and for steelmaking across South Yorkshire. I have been fighting for this plant since day one, with a determination to prevent our plant from becoming another casualty of industrial decline. Since Liberty's collapse, I have worked tirelessly alongside workers, unions and the local community to protect jobs and keep our plant's future alive. I'm proud that our Government has provided £50 million to pay the wages and pensions of our steelworkers in Stocksbridge and Rotherham, keeping our steelworks open. This will continue while the Government works towards public acquisition of Speciality Steel UK (SSUK), to secure a sustainable long-term future for SSUK as a speciality steelmaker, as well as opportunities for regeneration. For the 600 workers at Stocksbridge, this means certainty and security. They can now be assured of continued jobs, pay, pensions and a Government finally prepared to back British steelmaking rather than watch it wither after years of neglect. I will continue to press the Government to restart steelmaking at these sites, an ambition I know the Steel Minister shares for our plant. Steel is the beating heart of Stocksbridge. At its peak, our site produced 15% of global aerospace and defence steel, and restarting production will safeguard the specialist skills, product qualifications and customer accreditations that took decades to build, while creating new jobs and growth for the future. There is more work ahead to secure a sustainable long-term future, and I will be working with ministers every step of the way. Today shows what's possible when workers and Government pull together to reindustrialise communities like Stocksbridge. This process has always been about securing a responsible owner for these sites to protect them for a generation to come. I am delighted that the Government have today recognised that these sites could play a vital role in supporting the Government's modern Industrial Strategy, producing specialist steel for sectors including aerospace, defence and advanced manufacturing.

caption: I’m always here to help East Yorkshire residents with tricky problems, and an issue I’ve sadly seen in my inbox again and again is Capita’s appalling administration of public sector pensions. caption: How do we build a new Arsenal of Democracy for the Age of Insecurity? Andy Burnham writing in the Times today is bang on. Britain must rebuild its hard power. But that defence investment can do more than strengthen our Armed Forces. It can help rebuild British industry, create skilled jobs & strengthen our economic resilience So how do we develop Mr Burnham’s agenda into a plan for 21st century Arsenal of Democracy?  Today, conflict has changed. 50 years ago we understood conflict as a Cold War. Now three revolutions are reshaping the world. 1. We’ve moved from unipolarity to multipolarity. Power is no longer concentrated in Washington. China challenges US leadership. Russia seeks to overturn Europe’s security order. India, Turkey & other middle powers increasingly shape events in their own right 2. Conflict has become systemic. Wars are no longer fought only by soldiers. Conflict runs through trade, finance, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, cyber attacks, critical minerals, energy systems, satellites, supply chains and social media. Economic dependence is weaponised. 3. Competition has become permanent. The distinction between war and peace is disappearing. Strategic competition is becoming the normal condition of international politics. Success will depend less on preparing for the next war than on building economies resilient enough to withstand continuous pressure. That changes the task of government. It means: Economic security is now national security. If that diagnosis is right, Britain needs something bigger than a Defence Industrial Strategy. We need to build with allies a new Arsenal of Democracy. How?  1. Make economic security the organising principle of government. Trade, technology, energy, finance, defence and industrial strategy should no longer be treated as separate policies. They now form one strategic system. 2. Decide what Britain must always control. Before spending billions, Govt must define the sovereign capabilities Britain needs in these new times - from munitions and autonomous systems to semiconductors, critical minerals and resilient supply chains - and where trusted allies strengthen rather than weaken our resilience. 3. Turn procurement into Britain’s most powerful industrial policy. The real question isn’t simply how much we spend. It’s how we buy. Every defence programme should strengthen supply chains, support innovative firms, build advanced manufacturing & create exportable technologies. 4. Build an industrial alliance of democracies. The choice now is between strategic resilience and strategic vulnerability. So should build sovereign capability where essential and deepen industrial partnerships with trusted democratic allies everywhere else. 5. Govern this as a national mission. This isn’t just another departmental strategy. It needs ten-year plans, annual Growth Statements, clear metrics, parliamentary scrutiny and institutions capable of driving delivery over decades rather than electoral cycles
videoSummary: Liam Byrne MP argues for a modern industrial strategy to build a new Arsenal of Democracy in response to shifting global security threats. He outlines a five-point plan to integrate economic security with national defence and manufacturing capability.

constituency: Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North

caption: Grooving and grinding on the M25 to reduce noise pollution in Runnymede and Weybridge. This week I was able to join the National Highways team working to improve the surface of the M25 and see their latest work first hand grooving and grinding the concrete motorway. Our area has the largest stretch of concrete motorway which runs through residential areas in the country. This is made up of thousands of individual concrete slabs with sealed joints between, rather than the standard UK road surfacing of tarmac, and the design results in increased noise and wear and tear to vehicles, especially when the joints begin to degrade. National Highways has been undertaking a series of work in recent years to repair these joints and are now moving to the next stage of works, using a new technique of adding small grooves to the concrete surface which helps to improve traction. The first phase of the work repaired and narrowed the slab joints, which reduced noise and wear and tear and also protect the motorway from the effects of extreme weather, as the joints can expand and contract with changing temperatures. The second phase applies Next Generation Concrete Surfacing (NGCS) via specialized diamond grinding and grooving to cut traffic noise and improve grip. Trials have shown these works can deliver noise reductions of around 5dB, which could make a real difference for nearby residents, as well as reduce wear and tear on vehicles using the motorway. I am grateful to the team carrying out this work and delighted to see the progress being made on this important project to reduce noise pollution from the M25.
videoSummary: Two construction workers in high-visibility gear and hard hats stand next to heavy road-maintenance machinery at night under streetlights. It's why I've been pushing for stronger guarantees for young people through what I'm calling the Youth Triple Lock – making sure everyone has a route into education, training, or work. Today's announcement is a step in that direction. But there's more in this Budget that matters for families here: Energy bills are coming down. From April, levies are coming off bills, saving the average household around £150. For lower-income families, that rises to £300. Fuel duty is frozen. Rail fares are frozen. Prescription charges are frozen. That's real help with the cost of living. And child poverty is being tackled head on. The Two Child Limit is being scrapped, lifting 450,000 children out of poverty. Combined with free school meals expansion, this parliament is set to deliver the largest fall in child poverty on record. These are fair choices that make a real difference to people's lives. That's what this Budget delivers for our constituency.

caption: Many residents continue to have queries about the ongoing works on the A320, given the size of the project, the length of time it has already been underway and the disruption this causes on such a major route. New Holloway Hill roundabout The good news is works have been progressing through the summer. Temporary lights are in place on Guildford Road outside Salesian School to enable continued work on the new Holloway Hill roundabout, including the construction of a concrete slab to protect underground utility works for when the road reopens later this year. This has been timed to take place over the summer holidays to minimise disruption. Work is also progressing to move existing utilities install drainage pipes and begin building the north side of the new roundabout. Residents have reported that diversion signs were not in place during recent road closures to support this work, and I have raised this with Surrey County Council. St Peter's Roundabout More progress is visible at St Peter's Roundabout. I know many residents were frustrated by the length of time lane restrictions remained in place, so I am pleased to see the traffic lights now have been installed and are operational, with lane restrictions being removed. One lane remains closed on St Peter's Way due to works on the central reservation. Residents should note the traffic lights are now in operation continuously, unlike the previous system that only worked at peak hours, due to the increased capacity of the roundabout. Ottershaw Roundabout One area that has seen less progress is the Ottershaw roundabout. It is still expected that work here will resume in summer 2026 – however there haven’t been any recent updates. While it is important that surveys and measures are completed to ensure the protection of trees and wildlife on the western side of the site, it is also important that residents receive clear communication regarding the timeframe for the next steps of this project. I plan to meet with the construction team and Surrey County Council shortly and will press again for an update on this work. I would also encourage residents to visit Surrey County Council’s website for information on the A320 works, which is available here: https://www.surreycc.gov.uk/roads-and-transport/roadworks-and-maintenance/roadworks/our-roadworks/a320-north-of-woking-improvements. Alternatively, you can also raise any concerns you may have about the works by email at a320feedback@surreycc.gov.uk Of course, if you have any issues that you wish to raise with me, then you can do so at ben.spencer.mp@parliament.uk
videoSummary: A blue highway information sign details the upcoming A320 Highway Improvements Scheme in Surrey, managed by Graham. The sign notes that enabling works are scheduled to start in January 2026.

caption: 🌾 Back British Farming Day🌾 Today is a chance to celebrate our brilliant British farmers and growers – including those working across Penistone and Stocksbridge – and to recognise the vital contribution they make to our economy, our food security and our rural communities. Earlier this year, I brought together farmers from across our constituency for a Farmers’ Roundtable with the CLA at Round Green Deer Farm. It was really valuable to hear directly about some of the biggest challenges facing local arable and livestock farmers, including supply chain pressures, planning, fly-tipping and rural crime. One of the clearest messages from that meeting was the importance of better joined-up working between farmers, local councils and regional partners – making sure businesses can access the support, advice and opportunities they need to thrive. That is why I welcome the Government’s renewed focus on backing British farming. The Environment Secretary has today confirmed: 🚜 £230 million for the next window of the Sustainable Farming Incentive 🌱 £225 million for capital grants to support practical improvements on farms 💧 Continued investment to help farms become more resilient to drought and extreme weather 🤝 A commitment to work with farmers through the Farming Roadmap, recognising that food production, profitability and environmental protection must go hand in hand There is more to do, and I will keep making sure the voices of farmers across Penistone and Stocksbridge are heard. Later this year, I will also be bringing partners together for a roundtable focused on wildfire risk – another issue where the knowledge and experience of our farming and rural communities will be essential. I’m proud to back British farming – today and throughout the year. 🌾

caption: This week, the Government published its Annual Statement on National Resilience. While it sets out ambition, I remain concerned that it lacks the concrete action needed to prepare #britain for growing national security threats. Over the last few months, I have been focusing heavily on national resilience - our ability as a country to prepare for, respond to and recover from major emergencies, from floods and cyber attacks to threats against our critical national infrastructure. #Exmouth and Exeter East, like every community across the UK, depends on us being better prepared for future crises. I recently held a debate in Parliament on national resilience, where I argued that we need to have a more honest conversation about the challenges we face and what is required from both the state and the public. Whether it is protecting our energy and food supplies, supporting our emergency services, or ensuring we can respond to major incidents, preparedness must become a national priority.  I then travelled to #Denmark to learn from their approach. Like Britain, Denmark has enjoyed decades of peace at home, but it has taken practical steps to strengthen its resilience. Its Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness helps coordinate government efforts and engage wider society in preparing for future challenges. Resilience must be a whole-of-society effort. The #Government is right to recognise the importance of public engagement, but today’s statement still leaves too many unanswered questions about what will actually be done, who is responsible, and how progress will be measured.

caption: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Bill has now moved to the committee stage, where it will be examined in detail. caption: 🚗 SHADOW BUSINESS SECRETARY VISITS JLR 🚗 On Friday I was pleased to join Shadow Business Secretary, Andrew Griffith MP, for a visit to Jaguar Land Rover’s Classic site. JLR is a company that represents the very best of British engineering and one of the proud pillars of our economy here in the West Midlands. JLR isn’t just a car manufacturer. It supports over 30,000 direct jobs, fuels more than 100,000 across the wider supply chain, and contributes £18 billion to our national economy. It’s also a deep source of regional pride and identity for the West Midlands. During our visit, we met with senior executives to discuss the ongoing impact of the recent cyber attack, the ripple effects across the supply chain, and how we can protect the region’s automotive future. ⚠️ Last week, I wrote to the Business Secretary and the Chancellor, calling for an emergency loan guarantee scheme to support struggling suppliers and for greater clarity from the Government. I have been very clear, without action, the consequences could be deep and irreversible for the UK’s automotive industry. I have always said my priority was saving jobs and businesses. Yesterday the government announced the a commercially provided loan underwritten by the government. It was clear this was necessary to protect the supply chain and minimise the cost to the taxpayer. All the talk of furlough and buying parts, were in my view, not viable and would have cost too much. This way, the taxpayer will get its money back.  Do I think the government moved too slowly? 100%. They need to learn from this and be more nimble. We were when we were in government. What now? Well I will continue to work with JLR and suppliers to make sure they can get through this crisis.  But it is clear we need a long term solution to cyber security attacks - a better insurance mechanism like FloodRe which is not for profit and keeps premiums low. The future is here. It is our job as legislators, working with industry, to make sure we are ready.
videoSummary: Saqib Bhatti MP visits the Jaguar Land Rover Classic site alongside Andrew Griffith MP to discuss the impact of a recent cyber attack on the automotive supply chain. The video outlines his advocacy for an emergency loan guarantee scheme and proposes a long-term insurance mechanism to bolster regional cyber security.

caption: Everyone deserves a safe, secure, and affordable place to call home. 🏡 For too long, renters in Wolverhampton North East and across the country have faced constant uncertainty and an unfair housing market that heavily favoured the privileged few. I promised to fight for a fairer society, and I am proud to say that this Labour Government is delivering. We have completely overhauled Renters' Rights to put the power back in your hands. Here is exactly what we have introduced to protect our community: 🛑 No More Bidding Wars It is now completely illegal for landlords or agents to request, encourage, or accept rental offers above the set advertised price. 💰 Fair Upfront Costs You can no longer be priced out of moving. Landlords are now legally blocked from asking for more than one month’s rent up front. 🏠 End to “No-Fault” Evictions We have finally banned Section 21. You can no longer be kicked out of your home for no reason—all evictions will now require strict, valid grounds. 🗓️ Flexible Tenancies We are ending the trap of fixed-term tenancies. Moving forward, all tenancies will default to a monthly rolling contract, giving you the flexibility to move when it works for you. 🐾 Rights for Your Pets Pets are part of the family! Landlords must now fairly consider all pet requests and cannot unreasonably refuse them. ⏳ Longer Notice Periods If a landlord is ending a tenancy because they are selling the property, they are now legally required to give you at least four months' notice, giving you proper time to find your next home. This is about rebalancing the scales and raising living standards for everyone in Wolverhampton North East. If you are a renter in the constituency and need advice on how these new protections apply to you, my office is here to help. Please get in touch! 👇 📧 sureena.brackenridge.mp@parliament.uk 📞 01902 288465 #WolverhamptonNorthEast #RentersRights #LabourDelivers #FairerSociety #HousingReform
videoSummary: This carousel details the new renters rights introduced by the government to improve housing security and fairness for tenants. caption: All change please, all change. Yesterday I was really pleased to welcome the Secretary of State for Transport, Heidi Alexander, to Wolverhampton train station. There could hardly be a more fitting place to make an important announcement about the future of our railways: West Midlands Trains is coming into public ownership. For too long, our railways have been run primarily for the benefit of private shareholders rather than the passengers who rely on them. Public ownership means rail services run in the public interest, not for private profit. ✅Keeping fares affordable. ✅Simpler modern ticketing. ✅Reinvested profits. Rail services operated by West Midlands Trains will officially transfer to public ownership on 1st February, when the company’s current contract expires, and this transition will happen at no extra cost to the taxpayer. Our railways helped build Wolverhampton and the Black Country. From these tracks, early pioneers powered the industrial revolution and helped shape the modern world. We owe it to that history, and to future generations, to have a railway that works for the people it serves. For the failed experiment of privatisation, this really is the end of the line! All change, please. All change.

caption: Throughout October, I’ve been making sure Blackpool South’s voice continues to be heard loud and clear in Westminster. 🗣️ I raised the point that investment for South Shore can be used quickly and effectively to regenerate our high streets, and I was pleased that the Minister agreed to come and work with local residents and business owners on what they want to see for the area.  I also asked the Secretary of State how we can better support the people of South Shore, which remains one of the most deprived areas in the country, to ensure government investment truly reaches those who need it most. In Parliament, I pressed once again for a full, transparent and comprehensive inquiry into the grooming gang cases, something victims and communities deserve after years of unanswered questions. I also raised the urgent issue that too many young people in Blackpool who need SEND support are being sent miles away from home, when that care should be available right here in our town. Alongside that, I’ve launched my SEND survey to hear directly from parents, carers, educators, and young people with lived experience, so their voices shape the changes we need. And as Vice Chair of the Boxing APPG, I was proud to pay tribute to Ricky Hatton and wish his new foundation every success in raising awareness of mental health challenges and offering the support to those in need.  We know Blackpool South has so much potential, which is why I’ll keep fighting to make sure we get the investment, services and opportunities our community deserves.  There’s a lot more to do, but together we can build a brighter future for our town, and a better Blackpool for all. 🗼 #houseofcommons #parliament #blackpool #chriswebbmp
videoSummary: Chris Webb MP provides a video update on his recent parliamentary activities throughout October, focusing on his advocacy for Blackpool South. caption: Behind the Scenes at Sainsbury's Wednesfield It was great to go behind the scenes at Sainsbury's Wednesfield to meet colleagues and discuss jobs, skills and the role the store plays in our community. Employing around 160 colleagues, the store operates 24 hours a day and continues to grow, with loyal customers and increasing demand. The biggest takeaway from my visit was the fantastic career opportunities available. Deputy Store Manager Paul joined Sainsbury's at just 16 and has progressed into management, as the company prepares to relaunch its apprenticeship programme later this year. I also learned about the wide range of careers available beyond stores, many of which people simply don't know exist. The dedication of the Wednesfield team was particularly impressive. One colleague has completed 60 years' service, 12 have worked there for more than 30 years, and over half the workforce has been with Sainsbury's for at least a decade. We also discussed retail crime and the abuse faced by shop workers. It was encouraging to hear positive feedback about the partnership work at Bentley Bridge, which combines stronger enforcement with positive youth engagement through organisations like the Wolves Foundation. Thank you to Paul, Niamh and the whole team for such a warm welcome. I'm keen to continue working with local employers like Sainsbury's to create more opportunities for local people.

caption: Should we be taxing billionaires more? The answer is yes - to get growth rising. The average person earning £10m from wealth pays a lower effective rate of tax than someone on £35k. That's clearly not right. Landlords have been paying less tax than their tenants. CEOs have been paying less than their receptionists. This is bad for growth for three reasons. First, it means people with wealth don't invest, because they can just take the value out of their company via dividends.  Second, it means there is less local spending, because workers have less in their pockets.  And third, it means the Greater Southeast (where around half of millionaires live), benefits while the rest of the country loses out. I'm really proud that this government is taxing dividends, landlords, capital gains, and non-doms more. It raises revenue, yes. But it's also really good for growth. #UKPolitics #tax #ReformUK #economics #Labour

caption: I visited the historic Pot House Hamlet in Silkstone and the brilliant businesses there - one of my favourite places to visit in our constituency when I want to relax! Did you know that one of the first main activities on site was a 17th century glass works? The remains of the glassworks and pottery were excavated by English Heritage in 2003, who then deemed the site a National Ancient Monument! Tom Horsfield, who established the modern-day Pot House Hamlet, told me that this site in on the farm that has been in their family since 1939. When he was growing up, he decided he’d rather grow roses than raise chickens after his father bought him 1000 roses when he was 12 to sell! By the time he was 21, he was growing and selling 55,000 a year. Since then, the Pot House Hamlet has gone from strength to strength, with Tom and his family building each unit on the land. I visited some of the local businesses there, including Riley’s Potting Shed Café, Pookie Womenswear, Aroma Therapy candles, Joseph Alessandro Bespoke Jewellery, Berry’s Opticians, Body Revive, Rupert’s Dog Shop and Dog Grooming Spa, and Horsfields Plant Nursery. Each business provides excellent quality services and goods, and I’m keen to work further with the businesses to support them. Thank you so much to the Horsfield family for showing me around and to all the lovely businessowners and staff members that I had a chance to talk with when I was there.

caption: Honouring Wednesfield's history with a £500,000 investment in its future. 🚤🍻 A pleasure to visit The Boat with Ray Fellows from the @Wednesfield History Society to meet the new owners, Bav and Goady, with Goady proudly being a Wednesfield lad. The Boat has been part of Wednesfield's story since the 1800s, so it's fitting that, alongside its transformation, Ray will work with the owners to bring the history of both the pub and our village to life through artwork displayed throughout the venue. The owners are investing £500,000 to transform this once-derelict building, creating 25 local jobs and turning it into a unique destination with a traditional pub downstairs, a restaurant upstairs and space for up to 140 guests. With stunning views over the canal on one side and St Thomas' Church on the other, this investment has the potential to attract more visitors to Wednesfield Village, support our High Street and breathe new life into one of our most historic landmarks. I wish the whole team every success and look forward to seeing The Boat reopen. 🚤🍻 📜 A Little History of The Boat Inn The earliest known record of The Boat dates back to 1896, when Joseph Williams was registered as a beer retailer in Church Street. A licence historians believe refers to The Boat. Built in the early 1800s, the pub has welcomed generations of Wednesfield residents. It was later run by families including the Gumbleys, Tennants and the Betts family, who became well known for canal trips and brewing their own beer. For well over 200 years, The Boat has been part of Wednesfield's story. Thanks to this investment, it is beginning an exciting new chapter while celebrating the rich history that makes it such a special part of our community.

caption: Sir Keir Starmer has been a terrible Prime Minister, who lied to our country then did huge damage to jobs and livelihoods across East Yorkshire and beyond, so I am pleased he has today announced his resignation.  From his Family Farm Tax, National Insurance hikes, betraying our veterans and Armed Forces, choosing Putin’s oil and gas over our own North Sea jobs, trying to pay to give away British territory, and covering up his disgraceful Peter Mandelson choices, he’s shown my constituents just what ‘change’ under Labour really looks like. As well as causing unemployment to soar, in his short time as Prime Minister, he unbelievably let more small boat migrants into the UK than under any other PM, and he’s let over 56,000 criminals out of prison early. Yet Labour MPs only want to know who they can tax even more to hand out higher benefits. They forced their leadership to give up on modest welfare reforms and borrowed more – their national debt interest alone is as much as our defence and schools budgets combined. The welfare state has become chronically unaffordable and whoever is in charge will confront the same harsh national reality.  So I’m pleased Starmer is going, but Andy Burnham will be worse. Burnham has already u-turned on his views – on migrant benefits, rejoining the EU, women-only spaces, WASPI support, and Labour manifesto promises. Did you know that Burnham, as Health Secretary in 2009, oversaw the first NHS hospital to be privately managed by a private healthcare operator? Regardless of who is running their party, Labour choices and values are more tax and benefits, and not being on the side of hard-working people. Labour’s ideas remain unfit for the circumstances we face and until the government are honest about trade-offs and what the country can realistically pay for the instability will continue.  We cannot keep raising taxes without serious economic consequences. It is time to abandon Labour’s failed policies and pursue the bold sustained growth that only Kemi Badenoch and the Conservative Party has set out and will deliver.
videoSummary: Charlie Dewhirst MP delivers a scathing critique of Keir Starmer following the Prime Minister's resignation announcement. caption: Stockton will look like it's never looked before. You'll see Roseberry Topping with a coffee sitting outside overlooking an amphitheatre, watching a show. Some questions that have been asked:  - Will the area be secure? The area will fall under the town centre PSPO and there will be dedicated security for the site. Stockton Borough Council have funded extra enforcement for the town centre.  - When does Riverside Road reopen? After the launch event of the park, morning of 22nd June.  - Are there toilet and changing facilities in the park? Yes, there is a separate building for this.  - What events will we see in the park? There are facilities for pop-up food and drink offerings.  - How old is the play area suitable for? All age groups from toddlers upwards. There will also be 'totter trails' for younger children as well as a water play extension.  - How high is the new slide? The towers are ten metres high and the slide is six-metres. It's designed in a safe way but will certainly be exciting!  - Is anywhere else in the country building such an ambitious project? I don't think, no.  - Was the project delivered within budget? Yes. Thank you to everyone who came out to support the campaign. Your energy and commitment make a real difference. Teesside has always been a place of ingenuity and hard work. From the bridges we built to the industries that powered Britain, our communities have always shaped the country’s future. Now we’re building the next chapter. caption: 🚨 Encouraging News for Wolverhampton: Crime is Down 🚨 As your MP, I want to share some positive updates from Wolverhampton Police. Over the last 12 months, we have seen overall crime fall by more than 7% across our city. Most importantly, thanks to the tireless work of our local officers, we are seeing significant reductions in the crimes that most affect our communities. Thank you. 👮🙏 For the year to March 2026, the figures show: 🔪 Serious youth violence (under 25s) involving a knife: Down over 34% 🏠 Home burglaries: Down 31% 🛑 Robberies: Down 27% (and thefts from a person down 17%) 🚗 Vehicle thefts: Down 14% (and thefts from vehicles down 12%) Continuing the Fight Against Crime. While these figures are highly encouraging, I share the view of Wolverhampton Police's Chief Superintendent, Anthony Tagg: any single crime is one too many. We do not underestimate the devastating impact crime has on victims and the wider community. That is why the commitment to catching offenders and cutting crime continues 24/7. Here is what is happening on the ground to keep our streets safe: Targeted Operations: Initiatives like Operation Redfox and the Project Guardian Taskforce are aggressively combatting gang activity and youth violence. You will see targeted patrols in hotspot areas across the city, including Whitmore Reans, Staveley, East Park, Heath Town, and Bilston. Visible Local Policing: Every area of our city now has a Dedicated Neighbourhood Officer (DNO) providing a visible, reassuring presence alongside response officers and public protection units. Tackling Retail Crime: Specialist business crime officers are working directly with retailers and partners to identify, apprehend, and jail repeat shoplifters. Working Together for a Safer City. Our teams are working tirelessly to bring offenders to justice, but community intelligence is vital. We need your help to keep this positive momentum going. The more information the police receive, the better they can address the issues that concern you most. If you see something, please report it: 📞 Emergency: Always dial 999 📱 Non-Emergency: Call 101 or use the Live Chat on the police website. Together, we will…
videoSummary: This carousel highlights positive trends in local public safety by detailing significant reductions in crime rates across Wolverhampton over the past year. caption: We all know the postal service we're getting in B71, DY4, WS10 and WV14 isn't good enough - and now that I've visited the delivery office in Wednesbury I can see why. The posties are great and they work really hard, but there are more and more parcels and fewer and fewer letters, they are understaffed and they are working to an outdated model. All this means they're struggling. I made it clear to managers locally how angry I am on behalf of local people about the service. I saw too much mail at the office that hadn’t been delivered yet. This is a problem all over the country. Right now Royal Mail are rolling out a new way of working. West Brom delivery office went live on Monday, Tipton will be live next Monday, Wednesbury will be live in September and Wolverhampton sometime after that. I hope that this will start making a difference - but if it doesn’t I will go back and find out why. I'm off to visit Tipton delivery office in September, and I’ll be back to visit Wednesbury in a couple of weeks to see if the new model has made things better. Thanks to the posties, the reps from @CWUNews and the local managers who took time to talk to me.

caption: Fantastic session with the Purpose Coalition roundtable last week, looking at how we can smash the barriers to opportunity for our young people and build a stronger talent pipeline! 🚀 With nearly 1 million young people currently NEET, we had a vital, honest discussion with local businesses, education leaders, and community champions about how we bridge the skills gap and set the next generation up for success. Key takeaways: 🧽 Prioritising Soft Skills & Well-being: Isolation has hit our youth hard. Employers are looking beyond just grades—they want to see resilience, curiosity, and communication skills. 🧱 Early Engagement: We need to get into schools early. Love the "Ways to Work" model using fun, hands-on activities like Lego to introduce career skills to kids aged 8-18! 👷 Reforming Apprenticeships: Great to discuss the shifts to the Growth and Skills Levy, but we must ensure our advanced manufacturing and construction sectors aren't left behind. We also need to cut the red tape for our SMEs. 🪄 Make industries attractive again: From £200-a-day bricklaying roles to high-tech manufacturing, we need to use platforms like TikTok and online simulations to show young people the incredible earning potential in the trades. ♎ Fair Pay: Strong backing for apprentice pay equity—paying young people based on the value of their work, supported by government subsidies. We also heard an incredibly inspiring pitch from a local film student with Tourette's who is using media and an upcoming documentary to fight stigma and promote workplace inclusion. Highlighting diverse talent is exactly how we build confidence and aspiration. Huge thanks to Wolverhampton City College, our university partners, and all the local businesses who attended. Let's keep working together to unlock the potential right here in our community! 👏💼 #PurposeCoalition #YouthEmployment #SkillsForLife #Wolverhampton #Apprenticeships

caption: Yesterday I hosted my second Feltham, Hanworth and Bedfont Knife Crime and Community Safety Summit with Rise & Thrive and Perfectlly Imperfect. The recent two tragic deaths have deeply affected the local community and we know that a greater number of children and young people are at risk of being drawn into growing postcode gang hostility. It is our job to work with families and together across the community to keep young people safe and away from crime. The Summit, which will see further regular meetings follow through the year, brought together police, schools, community organisations, parents, the local council and the Mayor of London’s Violence Reduction Unit to build a shared understanding of the challenges, support how we further to respond to young people involved in criminality, how we work to protect local residents and shops from anti-social behaviour, and develop how we work together as a community and as agencies through a long-term strategy. Building relationships with young people at risk, taking weapons off our streets and creating pathways to young people building positive futures means offering young people more tailored support, mentoring and opportunities. This is the start of a sustained programme of work. We will continue building the partnerships, interventions and opportunities needed to protect our young people, support families and make Feltham, Hanworth and Bedfont safer for everyone.

caption: The Finance Bill (aka 'The Budget') made its way through the "Committee Stage" in the Houses of Commons. But what does that mean? The committee stage is a crucial, detailed, line-by-line examination of a bill that occurs after its second reading in the UK Parliament. It allows MPs to undertake scrutiny, debate on specific amendments, and suggest potential changes to the legislation. We do this as a "Public Bill Committee", and I was lucky enough to be part of one with fellow MPs from across parties. It means that the bill can now go onto the reports stage and its "Third Reading", where it can become an act! ...hope you all find this as exciting as I do. 🤓
